overviewHtml:
This graded quiz assesses your understanding of the evidence and arguments about AI's effects on information, fairness, and creative work. You'll be asked about documented harms from synthetic media, the evidence on elections, the liar's dividend, provenance and labeling, how bias enters AI systems, the COMPAS dispute, competing fairness definitions, the training-data dispute, the US court rulings, and settlements.

Note: Aim for a score of 80 percent or higher. If you score lower, use the feedback to review the topics you missed, then retake the quiz.

forms.stemHtml: Which harm from synthetic media can be established most firmly from the kind of evidence it leaves behind?

options.html: A slow decline in the public's confidence in news
options.text: A slow decline in the public's confidence in news
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: A shift in how a national electorate voted
options.text: A shift in how a national electorate voted
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: A firm's loss of money to a faked video call
options.text: A firm's loss of money to a faked video call
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A fraud has a victim, a loss, and a record, so investigators can establish what happened without estimating what millions of people believed.

options.html: A change in how voters feel about politics
options.text: A change in how voters feel about politics
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

forms.stemHtml: A review of the 2024 US presidential election found a lack of evidence that AI-enabled disinformation had a measurable impact on the result. How should that finding be read?

options.html: AI-generated content was proven to have no effect on any voter
options.text: AI-generated content was proven to have no effect on any voter
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: No effect on the outcome was shown, and data was limited
options.text: No effect on the outcome was shown, and data was limited
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The review said the lack of evidence was mainly due to insufficient data on real voter behavior, and that AI content did shape discussion.

options.html: AI-generated content was absent from the campaign
options.text: AI-generated content was absent from the campaign
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: The outcome was changed in ways the review chose not to report
options.text: The outcome was changed in ways the review chose not to report
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

forms.stemHtml: A mayor is caught on a genuine audio recording making an offensive remark. She says the recording was generated by AI, and some residents accept this because they know such audio can be faked. What is this an example of?

options.html: An influence operation
options.text: An influence operation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: Fraud by impersonation
options.text: Fraud by impersonation
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: The liar's dividend
options.text: The liar's dividend
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Real evidence is dismissed as fake, and the denial is believable because the public knows convincing fakes exist.

options.html: A provenance failure
options.text: A provenance failure
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements describe limits of provenance records and labels for AI-generated content? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Marks can be removed from a file
options.text: Marks can be removed from a file
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Metadata can be lost when a file is screenshotted, re-saved, or uploaded to a service that strips it.

options.html: A file with no mark isn't thereby genuine
options.text: A file with no mark isn't thereby genuine
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The absence of a label tells you nothing about whether content is real.

options.html: Many devices and services don't support the standards
options.text: Many devices and services don't support the standards
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Adoption is partial, and a record helps only if every step in a file's history supports it.

options.html: A provenance record can never be checked for tampering
options.text: A provenance record can never be checked for tampering
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on provenance and labeling.

forms.stemHtml: A health algorithm was meant to find the sickest patients. It predicted each patient's future health care cost and gave Black patients lower scores than equally sick white patients. Race was not an input. How did the bias get in?

options.html: Through a rule its builders wrote to lower some scores
options.text: Through a rule its builders wrote to lower some scores
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: Through inaccurate predictions of what patients cost
options.text: Through inaccurate predictions of what patients cost
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: Through records that left out most Black patients
options.text: Through records that left out most Black patients
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: Through cost, a proxy that tracked unequal access
options.text: Through cost, a proxy that tracked unequal access
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Less was spent on Black patients than on equally sick white patients, so predicting cost understated their needs. No intent and no race input were required.

forms.stemHtml: ProPublica reported that the COMPAS risk score wrongly flagged Black defendants as higher risk at nearly twice the rate of white defendants. The vendor replied that a given score meant the same for both groups. How can both statements be accurate?

options.html: Each side analyzed a different set of defendants
options.text: Each side analyzed a different set of defendants
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: Each side used a different measure of fairness
options.text: Each side used a different measure of fairness
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! ProPublica measured error rates by group. The vendor's defense was calibration. Both described the same records correctly.

options.html: One side's figures were later shown to be wrong
options.text: One side's figures were later shown to be wrong
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: The score was changed between the two analyses
options.text: The score was changed between the two analyses
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

forms.stemHtml: A 2016 proof showed that three reasonable fairness conditions for a risk score can't all hold when groups' base rates differ and prediction is imperfect. Which conclusions does the proof support? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Choosing which condition to satisfy is a value choice
options.text: Choosing which condition to satisfy is a value choice
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Mathematics shows that the conditions conflict and doesn't say which matters more.

options.html: Bias in a system can't be reduced by any means
options.text: Bias in a system can't be reduced by any means
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on competing definitions of fairness.

options.html: A calibrated score can still make unequal errors across groups
options.text: A calibrated score can still make unequal errors across groups
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! When base rates differ, a score that means the same for each group will have different error rates.

options.html: A system can be called fair by one definition and unfair by another
options.text: A system can be called fair by one definition and unfair by another
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each definition is a different statement of what must be equal across groups.

forms.stemHtml: What is the central question in the dispute between creators and AI developers over training data?

options.html: Whether AI models should be allowed to write books
options.text: Whether AI models should be allowed to write books
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Whether authors may use AI tools in their own writing
options.text: Whether authors may use AI tools in their own writing
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Whether training needs permission and payment
options.text: Whether training needs permission and payment
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Creators say using their works to train a model requires consent and compensation. Developers say training is a fair use.

options.html: Whether copyright should last for a shorter time
options.text: Whether copyright should last for a shorter time
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

forms.stemHtml: Which statements about US court rulings on AI and fair use, as of October 2026, are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: One court held training on books to be fair use and pirated copies not
options.text: One court held training on books to be fair use and pirated copies not
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That was the 2025 ruling in Bartz v. Anthropic.

options.html: One court ruled for a developer while saying the ruling didn't establish that training is lawful
options.text: One court ruled for a developer while saying the ruling didn't establish that training is lawful
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That was the 2025 ruling in Kadrey v. Meta, which turned on the authors' lack of evidence of market harm.

options.html: Courts held that a non-generative tool competing with the works it copied wasn't fair use
options.text: Courts held that a non-generative tool competing with the works it copied wasn't fair use
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! That was Thomson Reuters v. Ross, decided in 2025 and affirmed on appeal in 2026.

options.html: The Supreme Court has ruled that AI training is a fair use
options.text: The Supreme Court has ruled that AI training is a fair use
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair use in US courts.

forms.stemHtml: An AI developer settles a class action brought by authors for 1.5 billion dollars. What does the settlement establish about the law on AI training?

options.html: That training on books is unlawful everywhere
options.text: That training on books is unlawful everywhere
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: Nothing binding; it is an agreement
options.text: Nothing binding; it is an agreement
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A settlement ends a lawsuit without a final court ruling on who was right, and it sets no precedent.

options.html: That every developer must pay the same amount
options.text: That every developer must pay the same amount
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: That training on books is lawful everywhere
options.text: That training on books is lawful everywhere
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

forms.stemHtml: An employee joins a video call with what appear to be senior colleagues and then transfers company money to fraudsters. The colleagues were deepfakes. Why can a case like this be documented in detail?

options.html: It has a victim, a loss, and a record
options.text: It has a victim, a loss, and a record
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A named firm was harmed, money left its accounts, and there are bank transfers and a police report to examine.

options.html: Deepfake fraud is the most common crime
options.text: Deepfake fraud is the most common crime
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: The firm's computer systems were broken into
options.text: The firm's computer systems were broken into
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: Researchers surveyed everyone who saw the call
options.text: Researchers surveyed everyone who saw the call
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

forms.stemHtml: A headline reads, "Study proves AI fakes had no influence on voters in 2024." The study it describes reported a lack of evidence of a measurable impact on the election result. What does the headline get wrong?

options.html: The study found that AI fakes decided the result
options.text: The study found that AI fakes decided the result
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: The study was about a different country's election
options.text: The study was about a different country's election
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: The study found that no AI fakes were made at all
options.text: The study found that no AI fakes were made at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: A lack of evidence isn't proof of no effect
options.text: A lack of evidence isn't proof of no effect
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The review said its data on voter behavior was insufficient. An absence of evidence produced by weak measurement is weaker than a careful search that found nothing.

forms.stemHtml: What does the liar's dividend require in order to operate?

options.html: A fake that many people have seen and believed
options.text: A fake that many people have seen and believed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: A law that forbids the labeling of AI content
options.text: A law that forbids the labeling of AI content
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: A fake so well made that experts can't detect it
options.text: A fake so well made that experts can't detect it
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: Public awareness that convincing fakes exist
options.text: Public awareness that convincing fakes exist
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! No fake has to be made or believed. The liar benefits because the public knows fakes are possible, so real evidence can be called fake.

forms.stemHtml: You find a striking photograph online. It carries no Content Credentials and no AI label. Which conclusions are justified? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The photograph is a genuine, unedited image
options.text: The photograph is a genuine, unedited image
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on provenance and labeling.

options.html: The missing label tells you nothing either way
options.text: The missing label tells you nothing either way
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Content made with a tool that doesn't mark its output, or with the mark removed, carries no label.

options.html: A record may have been stripped when the file was shared
options.text: A record may have been stripped when the file was shared
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Metadata is often lost when a file is re-saved or uploaded.

options.html: The device or software that made it may not support the standard
options.text: The device or software that made it may not support the standard
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Adoption of provenance standards is incomplete.

forms.stemHtml: A lender removes applicants' race from the data used by its loan-approval model. The model still approves one racial group far less often. Which explanation fits how bias is known to enter such systems?

options.html: Another input acts as a proxy for race
options.text: Another input acts as a proxy for race
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Removing a characteristic from the inputs doesn't stop other inputs from carrying its effect, as cost did in the health algorithm and a single word did in the recruiting tool.

options.html: The model secretly recovered the deleted data
options.text: The model secretly recovered the deleted data
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: The lender's staff must have intended the result
options.text: The lender's staff must have intended the result
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: Models can't be accurate without using race
options.text: Models can't be accurate without using race
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

forms.stemHtml: One article says, "COMPAS was shown to be biased." Another says, "COMPAS was shown to be fair." What does each article leave out?

options.html: The name of the company that sold the score
options.text: The name of the company that sold the score
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: The number of defendants in the data
options.text: The number of defendants in the data
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: The year in which the analysis was done
options.text: The year in which the analysis was done
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: The measure of fairness it relies on
options.text: The measure of fairness it relies on
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! By error rates the score treated groups unequally. By calibration it treated them alike. A claim that names its measure can be checked.

forms.stemHtml: A risk score is calibrated: a "high risk" label means the same chance of the outcome in Group A and Group B. The outcome is more common in Group A. Which statements must be true, unless prediction is perfect? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The score's error rates will differ between the groups
options.text: The score's error rates will differ between the groups
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! With different base rates and imperfect prediction, calibration and balanced error rates can't both hold.

options.html: Evening out the error rates would break calibration
options.text: Evening out the error rates would break calibration
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Adjusting the labels to balance errors makes a label mean something different in each group.

options.html: The score must have used group membership as an input
options.text: The score must have used group membership as an input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on competing definitions of fairness.

options.html: Someone has to decide which condition to give up
options.text: Someone has to decide which condition to give up
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The conflict forces a choice, and the mathematics doesn't make it.

forms.stemHtml: An author says, "They should have asked me and paid me before using my novel." A developer says, "Training creates something new and doesn't replace your novel." What are they disagreeing about?

options.html: Whether training requires a license
options.text: Whether training requires a license
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The author's position is consent and compensation through licensing. The developer's position is that training is a transformative fair use that needs no license.

options.html: Whether the novel is protected by copyright
options.text: Whether the novel is protected by copyright
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Whether the novel was used in training at all
options.text: Whether the novel was used in training at all
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Whether the author wrote the novel alone
options.text: Whether the author wrote the novel alone
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

forms.stemHtml: A headline says, "US courts have ruled that AI training is legal." Which facts, as of October 2026, show that the headline overstates the rulings? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: One judge who ruled for a developer wrote that his ruling didn't establish that training is lawful
options.text: One judge who ruled for a developer wrote that his ruling didn't establish that training is lawful
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! He said it stood only for the point that the authors made the wrong arguments and lacked evidence.

options.html: One court held that keeping pirated copies of books wasn't fair use
options.text: One court held that keeping pirated copies of books wasn't fair use
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The same order that found training to be fair use sent the pirated copies to trial.

options.html: Every court that has considered the question has ruled against developers
options.text: Every court that has considered the question has ruled against developers
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair use in US courts.

options.html: The rulings favoring developers came from trial courts and don't bind other courts
options.text: The rulings favoring developers came from trial courts and don't bind other courts
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! They decide the cases before them, and the Supreme Court hasn't ruled.

forms.stemHtml: An author says, "The 1.5 billion dollar settlement proves that training AI on books is illegal." What is wrong with this statement?

options.html: The settlement was later rejected by the court
options.text: The settlement was later rejected by the court
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: The settlement was about images, not books
options.text: The settlement was about images, not books
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: The settlement paid nothing to any author
options.text: The settlement paid nothing to any author
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: A settlement doesn't decide what the law is
options.text: A settlement doesn't decide what the law is
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! It is an agreement between the parties. In that case the court's ruling that training was a fair use was left in place, and the settlement arose from the pirated copies.

forms.stemHtml: Fraud, impersonation, and sexual imagery made without consent are the best-documented harms from synthetic media. What do these harms have in common that effects on public opinion usually lack?

options.html: They are caused by a single company's products
options.text: They are caused by a single company's products
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: They are counted in full by official statistics
options.text: They are counted in full by official statistics
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: They affect very large numbers of people at once
options.text: They affect very large numbers of people at once
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on synthetic media and documented harms.

options.html: An identifiable victim and a traceable loss
options.text: An identifiable victim and a traceable loss
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Each case has someone who was harmed, something that was lost, and a record of it. How often such cases occur is less certain.

forms.stemHtml: Which statement about AI-generated content and election outcomes is best supported by research so far?

options.html: No change in an outcome has been demonstrated
options.text: No change in an outcome has been demonstrated
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Research finds little evidence that AI-generated content has changed election outcomes, while subtler effects haven't been well measured.

options.html: Outcomes in several countries have been reversed
options.text: Outcomes in several countries have been reversed
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: Subtle and delayed effects have been ruled out
options.text: Subtle and delayed effects have been ruled out
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

options.html: Voters are unaffected by false content of any kind
options.text: Voters are unaffected by false content of any kind
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on AI and elections.

forms.stemHtml: Which of these cases fits the liar's dividend?

options.html: An executive calls an authentic leaked video a deepfake
options.text: An executive calls an authentic leaked video a deepfake
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The liar's dividend is the benefit gained by dismissing real evidence as fake when the public knows fakes exist.

options.html: A fabricated video of an executive is believed by investors
options.text: A fabricated video of an executive is believed by investors
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: A scammer clones an executive's voice to request a payment
options.text: A scammer clones an executive's voice to request a payment
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

options.html: A website removes the label from an AI-generated video
options.text: A website removes the label from an AI-generated video
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the liar's dividend.

forms.stemHtml: A commentator says, "Once every AI tool labels its output, we'll always know what's real." Which facts count against this claim? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: Labels and watermarks can be removed or weakened
options.text: Labels and watermarks can be removed or weakened
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A mark that can be stripped doesn't travel reliably with the content.

options.html: Some tools won't mark their output at all
options.text: Some tools won't mark their output at all
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Adoption is partial, and legal duties apply only in some jurisdictions.

options.html: Provenance records make genuine photographs less trustworthy
options.text: Provenance records make genuine photographs less trustworthy
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on provenance and labeling.

options.html: Unmarked content can't be assumed to be authentic
options.text: Unmarked content can't be assumed to be authentic
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The absence of a label is not evidence that content is real.

forms.stemHtml: A company says its hiring tool can't be biased against women because it is never told an applicant's sex. What do the documented cases of bias show about this claim?

options.html: It is correct, since bias requires a sensitive input
options.text: It is correct, since bias requires a sensitive input
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: It is correct, as long as the tool is accurate overall
options.text: It is correct, as long as the tool is accurate overall
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

options.html: It is unsafe, since other inputs can track sex
options.text: It is unsafe, since other inputs can track sex
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! An experimental recruiting tool trained on past résumés marked down the word "women's" without being given applicants' sex.

options.html: It is unsafe, since such tools are built with intent to harm
options.text: It is unsafe, since such tools are built with intent to harm
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on how bias enters AI systems.

forms.stemHtml: In the dispute over the COMPAS risk score, what did ProPublica and the vendor disagree about?

options.html: Which facts make a score fair
options.text: Which facts make a score fair
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both sides' figures were accurate. One pointed to unequal error rates, the other to scores that meant the same for each group.

options.html: Whether the defendants had reoffended
options.text: Whether the defendants had reoffended
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: Whether race was asked on the questionnaire
options.text: Whether race was asked on the questionnaire
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

options.html: Whether judges ever saw the scores
options.text: Whether judges ever saw the scores
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the COMPAS findings.

forms.stemHtml: An engineer says, "Give us enough time and we'll build a score that satisfies every reasonable definition of fairness." Which statements about this promise are accurate? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: It can't be kept when base rates differ and prediction is imperfect
options.text: It can't be kept when base rates differ and prediction is imperfect
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! A 2016 proof showed that three reasonable fairness conditions can't all hold except in special cases.

options.html: The obstacle is mathematical, so more engineering won't remove it
options.text: The obstacle is mathematical, so more engineering won't remove it
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The conflict follows from the arithmetic of the definitions.

options.html: It fails because all scoring systems are equally unfair
options.text: It fails because all scoring systems are equally unfair
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on competing definitions of fairness.

options.html: Improving the data or the target can still reduce bias
options.text: Improving the data or the target can still reduce bias
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The proof doesn't say bias can't be reduced. It says the fairness conditions can't all be met at once.

forms.stemHtml: If the creators' position in the training-data dispute prevailed, what would AI developers have to do before training on a copyrighted book?

options.html: Prove that the model can't reproduce the book
options.text: Prove that the model can't reproduce the book
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Wait until the book's copyright has expired
options.text: Wait until the book's copyright has expired
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Publish the full list of books used in training
options.text: Publish the full list of books used in training
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on the training-data dispute.

options.html: Obtain a license from the rights holder
options.text: Obtain a license from the rights holder
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The creators' position is that training requires consent and compensation, and that licensing is the way to provide them.

forms.stemHtml: A headline says, "US courts have ruled that AI training is theft." Which facts, as of October 2026, show that the headline overstates the rulings? (Select all that apply.)

options.html: The ruling against fair use involved a non-generative tool
options.text: The ruling against fair use involved a non-generative tool
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Both the trial court and the appeals court in Thomson Reuters v. Ross distinguished it from generative AI.

options.html: Two trial courts found training generative models on books to be fair use on the records before them
options.text: Two trial courts found training generative models on books to be fair use on the records before them
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! Those were the 2025 rulings in Bartz v. Anthropic and Kadrey v. Meta.

options.html: The tool in the ruling against fair use competed directly with the works it copied
options.text: The tool in the ruling against fair use competed directly with the works it copied
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The court found that the developer meant to build a market substitute.

options.html: No court has found any copying by an AI developer to be unlawful
options.text: No court has found any copying by an AI developer to be unlawful
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on fair use in US courts.

forms.stemHtml: A developer says, "We settled with authors, so the question of training on their books is closed for good." The settlement covers past copying up to a fixed date. What does the developer's statement overlook?

options.html: Future conduct and model outputs remain open
options.text: Future conduct and model outputs remain open
options.feedbackHtml: Correct! The settlement resolves past claims by agreement. It doesn't release claims about what the models produce or about anything done later.

options.html: Settlements must be renewed every single year
options.text: Settlements must be renewed every single year
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: Authors can cancel a settlement whenever they like
options.text: Authors can cancel a settlement whenever they like
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

options.html: A settlement applies only outside the United States
options.text: A settlement applies only outside the United States
options.feedbackHtml: Sorry, that's incorrect. Review the reading on licensing and settlements.

title: Information, Fairness, and Creative Rights
